Live runtime state on the Behavior Tree

Three backend↔frontend contracts (still open), the state model they share, and the rendering language Zach decided on 2026-09-05 — Groot2’s transition-log model, Flowstate’s sampled palette and group aggregation, spinners on the whole active path, the marching-dash active-path edge — implemented, photographed, and tested in the clickable mock-backend lab on real chrome, before any real backend exists.
2026-09-05 · repo at 71f40082 · facts measured from the tree at build time by docs/build_behavior_tree_runtime_viz_proposal.py

01The frame, and one correction to it

The ask decomposes into four independently decidable layers, and that decomposition is the right one — it is also exactly how the two reference ecosystems are built (§02): (1) a state model — what runtime state is, per node; (2) rendering — how the canvas paints it; (3) the backend contract — how state travels from an executing tree into the app; (4) a mock backend — so layers 1–2 ship and demo before layer 3 has a real producer.

One assumption deserves a push before proposals: “editing the XML file that then hot-reloads” put the canonical document forward as a candidate carrier. Every reference implementation refuses that — Groot2’s wire never touches the authored file, py_trees’ visitors “should not modify the behaviours they visit,” and this repo’s own boundary says the same:

“I don’t want to do any deriving logic within the whiteboard… whiteboard should remain like this hackable thing for drawing things… when we use it for rendering the python code, it’s the python that is really driving a lot of it.” Zach, PROJECT — System Sketch (the whiteboard-stays-dumb boundary, 2026-09-03)

Runtime status is ephemeral, high-frequency, derived data; the .systemsketch file is authored content behind a SHA-256 CAS fence with a conflict UI (the draw.io-alignment report, 2026-09-03). Pushing ticks through that channel would make every tick a document revision, trip the fence against the person’s own unsaved edits, and persist run state into saved boards. So the honest version of the file-shaped candidate is a sibling run file — proposal P1 — and the XML itself is never the carrier in any proposal. Everything else in the frame stands.

02Prior art, verified at the source

Groot2 / BehaviorTree.CPP — the ecosystem this feature’s XML already speaks

  • The tree process is the server. Groot2Publisher binds ZeroMQ REP :1667 + PUB :1668; Groot2 is a client (groot2_publisher.cpp).
  • Structure travels once; status is a poll, not a push. The instantiated tree is serialized to XML in memory once (every node stamped with a _uid); STATUS returns one flat uid+status buffer for the whole tree, overwritten in place, at whatever cadence the client asks. The only pushed message is “breakpoint reached.”
  • The wire never touches the file on disk. Confirmed by reading the publisher end to end — no filesystem I/O exists in it.
  • IDLE remembers. A node returning to idle is encoded 10 + previous_status so the UI can keep showing what it last returned — precedent for outcome-that-decays rather than outcome-that-vanishes.
  • Replay is an event log. FileLogger2’s .btlog = XML header + 9-byte records (t·µs, uid, status); Groot2 scrubs by folding records up to the cursor. A bounded in-memory deque (TOGGLE_RECORDING/GET_TRANSITIONS) is the live twin of the same shape.
  • Mocking is official. TestNode (async_delay + scripted result) + wildcard substitution rules loadable from JSON fake a tree without editing it; Groot2 PRO adds live breakpoints and forced SUCCESS/FAILURE injection. No stock probability knob.

py_trees — the Python runtime the backend will actually be

  • Two-layer model is canonical: authored structure vs a per-tick dict {uuid → Status} captured by a SnapshotVisitor (plus the previous tick’s dict, so preemption paints as INVALID). Visitors are read-only by contract (visualisation, visitors module).
  • The wire is whole-tree snapshots, change-gated. py_trees_ros re-serializes every node each publish with is_active flags; publishes only when something changed (or a period elapses). Deltas: never. Structure edits are just a snapshot with changed=True.
  • py_trees_js (its web viewer) receives full-snapshot JSON per tick and keeps a client-side cache with rewind/resume — a scrubber over received frames, exactly the lab’s shape.
  • The dummy kit exists but split: TickCounter (n ticks then a chosen status), ProbabilisticBehaviour (weighted SUCCESS/FAILURE/RUNNING), StatusQueue (scripted), Periodic, SuccessEveryN. The lab’s per-node {durationTicks, pSuccess} is TickCounter × ProbabilisticBehaviour composed — the two stock pieces in one knob.

Intrinsic Flowstate — the Process view’s UX oracle already has this feature

Convergent verdict from all three: authored structure + a separate per-tick status overlay joined on one stable node identity, snapshots over deltas, replay as an event fold, and simulation as a first-class target. Nobody writes status into the definition.

03What the app already owns (measured at build time)

  • The identity key exists: every projected child is stamped btPath (0.2.1-style index paths; meta keys btRegion, btPath, btRole). The Flowstate frame projects 24 children in the Tree view, 12 in Process — same paths in both, so one status map paints every projection. The analog of Groot2’s _uid, already shipped.
  • The document channel is deliberately heavyweight: WATCH_INTERVAL_MS = 1500 poll, SHA-256 digest CAS, atomic replace, conflict UI. Right for boards; wrong for ticks — which is the architectural argument, not just taste.
  • An ephemeral-store pattern is already in the codebase: src/recorder/recorderStore.ts — module store + useSyncExternalStore, installed from onMount, never in the tldraw store. Runtime state copies this, because the tldraw store is the document: status written into shape props/meta would autosave into boards.
  • The host has room for a run lane: scripts/server.py currently serves /api/health /api/preview-clone /api/promoted-workspace /api/recordings /api/recordings/arm /api/recordings/last /api/recordings/status /api/release /api/workspace/directory /api/workspace/file /api/workspace/list /api/workspace/rename /api/workspace/reveal /api/workspace/stat /api/workspace/trash — a bounded-HTTP, single-origin loopback controller. A /api/bt/run/* family is the same dialect.
  • Scrubber precedent in-app: src/history/HistoryList.tsx (element history) and the vault’s trace-viewer shape (filmstrip + event lanes on one clock).
  • Found while building this: a Behavior Tree region’s SVG/PNG export silently drops the region’s own layer (wires, Start, header) — child cards only. Flagged as its own fix; the lab replays the painted DOM’s geometry instead.

04The three contracts

P1 · Run sidecar file, watched the file-shaped candidate, made honest

Backend: the runner (a py_trees post-tick handler, ~15 lines) writes <board>.run.json — one whole RunSnapshot (§05), atomic tmp+rename, debounced to ~10 Hz. Frontend: a second stat-poll on the sidecar (the document watcher’s own pattern, faster interval), parse on digest change, feed the store.

For: zero new transport; works when app and runner share only a filesystem (SSH mounts, containers); trivially inspectable (cat the run). Against: latency floor = poll interval + write cadence; disk churn for something never meant to persist; no history unless it grows into P3; two runners clobber one file; and it quietly re-couples runtime to the document’s directory. Fidelity: snapshots only — transitions between polls are lost (same loss Groot2 accepts on its STATUS channel).

P2 · A run channel on the Preview host recommended

Backend: the runner POSTs {runId, xmlDigest, frames:[…]} batches to /api/bt/run after each tick (the SnapshotVisitor→JSON adapter is ~20 lines of Python; any language can speak it). The host keeps, per run: latest snapshot + a bounded ring of transitions — Groot2’s STATUS buffer and its recording deque, as one lane. Frontend: GET /api/bt/run/latest?since=tick on a 150–250 ms poll (304 when unchanged), store, overlay. SSE is a later transport swap behind the same client function, not a different contract.

For: this is the reference architecture — Groot2 live monitoring is literally a client-cadence poll of a snapshot buffer, and py_trees_ros is change-gated whole-tree snapshots; no artifact files invented; multiple consumers free (a second browser, an agent asking “what failed last run?”); GET /api/bt/run/<id>/trace falls out of the ring and subsumes P3’s replay. The host is already the app’s one loopback authority. Against: needs the host running (the embedded IDE case needs its own lane later); one new endpoint family to maintain.

Fidelity: snapshots for liveness plus the transition ring for completeness — the only proposal that keeps both.

P3 · Trace-first: the run is a file of transitions the walking/replay lane

Backend: the runner appends JSONL transition records {t, tick, path, to} (the .btlog shape, readable form) to runs/<stamp>.btrace.jsonl; a run is an artifact you can commit, attach to a bug, or have an agent produce in CI. Frontend: open a trace (or tail a growing one), fold events into frames, scrub — live is just the cursor pinned to the tail.

For: nails “stepping through / walk it”; replay and diffing runs are first-class; transport-free; the vault’s trace-viewer shape and Groot2’s own offline story. Against: as the only channel, live latency and lifecycle (which file is live? cleanup?) get awkward; every consumer re-implements the fold.

Recommendation: P2, with P3’s event log as its memory — the host’s ring is a trace, exposed at /trace, so scrubbing and run artifacts come free; P1 survives as a degraded-transport fallback (same RunSnapshot JSON written to a file) for contexts with no host. The deciding facts: the reference implementation Zach named is already a poll-a-snapshot design, so P2 loses nothing to “real push”; and only P2 serves both consumers this app actually has — a human watching live, and agents/CI asking questions after the fact. Reversible: the store’s input is the state model, not the transport, so switching contract later rewrites one client module.

05The state model all three share

// Layer 1 — the contract that actually gets settled. Everything joins on btPath.
type BtNodeStatus =
  'fresh' | 'running' | 'success' | 'failure' | 'halted'   // halted ≈ py_trees INVALID / Groot2 IDLE_FROM_*

interface BtRunSnapshot {
  runId: string          // one execution of one tree
  xmlDigest: string      // sha256 of the canonical XML — a run against
                         // edited XML is visibly stale, never misdrawn
  treeId: string
  tick: number
  at: number             // wall-clock ms
  statuses: Record<string /* btPath */, { status: BtNodeStatus; sinceTick: number }>
  visited: string[]      // this tick's traversal, in order — wire glow + Start flash
  outcome: 'success' | 'failure' | null
  blackboard?: Record<string, string>   // later; py_trees sends visited keys per tick
}

interface BtRunEvent {                 // the CANONICAL record (decided 2026-09-05):
  seq: number                          // frames above are folds of a list of these;
  tick: number; at: number             // tick + timestamp let a scrubber rebuild the
  path: string                         // exact state at ANY tick — or step INSIDE one
  from: BtNodeStatus; to: BtNodeStatus
}

In-app it lives in a runtime store beside the editor, never inside it (the recorder-store pattern): the tldraw store is the document, and the digest fence exists precisely to protect it from non-authored writes. BehaviorTreeCanvas already knows every node’s rect per projection, so rendering subscribes by region + path and paints — no production shape gains a runtime prop.

06Rendering: the decided language, proven in the lab on real chrome

Decided 2026-09-05 (Zach, after the UX survey), implemented in the lab the same day:

  • Groot2’s model is the base. Status is painted as color/state (no icon system); the history is transition-based, not tick-based — the canonical record is {seq, tick, at, path, from, to} and frames are derived by folding it, which is exactly the fix for py_trees’ “skips through ticks” feeling. The scrubber’s detail view is Groot2’s real Transitions table (Time · Node · Status, filterable, current row highlighted).
  • Flowstate’s palette, verbatim — the survey’s sampled values: running #E2D9FC (border #8b5cf6), done #CAFCD0, pending/untaken #DEDEDE, idle = neutral chrome. Failure keeps Groot2’s #dc2626 (Flowstate never shows failure publicly). Group aggregation copied exactly: running tints the header lavender; success turns the header mint and washes the whole surface pale green — children keep their own fills, untaken branches stay gray. Outcomes persist for the run; re-execution clears them, never a timer (so the earlier Monitor-decay mode is gone).
  • The spinner rides the whole active path — Zach’s stated improvement over Flowstate: “everything that is purple in Intrinsic Flowstate would have a spinner.” Every RUNNING ancestor (and a running group’s header) carries MoveIt’s rotating dotted ring, not just the ticking leaf.
  • The active path is an animated marching dash from Start to the current node — Zach’s explicit call, overriding the survey’s recommendation against a dashed running edge. The collision it warned about (dash already means async/delayed on this app’s cables) is resolved on a different channel: the cable vocabulary is a static dash pattern; the active path visibly moves. A screenshot of an async cable is identical from moment to moment; the live path never is. The lab draws this contract into the scene (the edge-vocabulary inset) and its test asserts it in pixels.

07The mock backend (“walk it”), and where its ideas come from

The lab’s driver is a ~120-line BT.CPP-semantics interpreter (Sequence/Fallback with memory, Parallel with success/failure counts, halt cascades) over the same canonical XML the region stores, with per-leaf {durationTicks, pSuccess} — py_trees’ TickCounter × ProbabilisticBehaviour composed, the knob BT.CPP’s TestNodeConfig (async_delay + scripted result) stops just short of. Seeded RNG makes every walk replayable (the report’s screenshots are a seed scan choosing seed 34 so the captured run tells the recovery story). Presets: Nominal, Flaky gripper, Chaos. Every status change appends to the canonical transition log; the scrubber folds the log — to any tick via the slider, or to any single transition via «/» and the table — and the driver’s own per-tick snapshots survive only as the independent oracle the fold is verified against, after every run and in docs/labs/test_bt_runtime_lab.mjs.

When the real backend lands, this driver is deleted and nothing else changes: it produces the same frames the wire would. A real py_trees run mocks even better than random numbers — swap leaves for StatusQueue/TickCounter behaviours via the same substitution idea BT.CPP ships, and the “draft sim” is a real tree, fake actuators — Flowstate’s Execute on: Simulation exactly.

09Decision surface

Decided since this report was first built (2026-09-05, later the same day): the rendering layer is no longer a proposal. Zach picked Groot2’s model (color-state painting, transition-based history, the Transitions table), Flowstate’s exact palette and group aggregation, spinners on the whole active path, and the animated marching-dash active-path edge (his call, overriding the survey’s dash-collision worry — resolved by the motion-vs-static channel, §06). All of it is implemented and tested in the lab; §06 shows the result. The transport contract below remains open — nothing here builds P1/P2/P3.

Done and proved here: the three contracts with the reference architectures verified at source; the shared state model with the transition log as the canonical record; the decided rendering language demonstrated on real chrome; a walkable, configurable mock backend with its own 38-check acceptance test. Not done, deliberately: no production code touched — no store, no endpoints, no overlay in src/; that is the implementation this proposal exists to de-risk. Also out of scope by choice: blackboard-value display per tick (py_trees defines the wire shape when wanted) and the IDE-host transport case.

  • The contract: adopt P2 (host run-channel, snapshot + transition ring, poll-first)? Default if silent: build the state model + store + overlay against the mock first — that work is identical under all three contracts — and cut the host lane when the first real runner needs it.
  • Transport ergonomics: poll-first (150–250 ms, 304-on-unchanged), SSE as a later swap? Default: yes; the reference tools are polls, and the client function hides it.
  • Where does the real runner live? A py_trees adapter Zach imports in his Python, or a host-side “run this board’s tree” button? Default: the adapter first (whiteboard stays dumb; Python drives), the button later as sugar over the same POST.
  • Transport strip placement: Flowstate docks run/stop/step on the region header — adopt that as the run-mode chrome? Default: yes, next to the projection pill, only while a run/mock is attached.
